question: May a replacement for the NFL week board's player distributions (nfl_dfs_sim.simulate_game, the continuous model measured overconfident) take its place, with the owner's sign-off?
candidates: research/data/nfl_wb_dist/candidates.json (A the constrained simulator as fitted on 2022-24; B the discrete allocation, quarterback term k; C production with a per-position x statistic quantile map)
seeds: game i of the sample in (season, week, game key) order: production random.seed(1000 + i); A and B numpy default_rng(1000 + i); the randomized PIT's uniform a crc32 of the player-week and statistic

sample.rule: every 2026 regular-season game of weeks 14-18 in research/data/player_weeks_2026.csv.gz once it is rebuilt by research/hist_data.py after the read date (Sleeper's weekly projections and box scores, the development table's own source): QB / RB / WR / TE with a projection and a kept box. Week 13 is EXCLUDED whole: its Thanksgiving and Friday games had kicked off before this registration, and the table carries no kickoff time to split it.
sample.extension_rule: if fewer than 60 games arrive, the read waits for 2027 weeks 1-6 (the same rule, research/data/player_weeks_2027.csv.gz) and pools them
sample.other_tests_on_these_games: the coaching registrations (R1, R2-H1, the coaching DFS read) also read 2026 weeks 13-18. They test different models and questions (game-flow engines, not per-player box distributions) and are NOT this test's family: no multiplicity correction is shared; the dependence (the same games) is acknowledged.

primary: for each candidate: the per-line log-loss gain over production, pooled over every scored line (the lines of candidates.json: off the projection only) and clustered by game -- sum over games of (production's log loss - the candidate's) / sum of lines, its SE the game-cluster ratio estimator's; z = gain / SE
holm: one-sided, family-wise 5% over the three candidates: the largest z must clear 2.128, the next 1.960, the third 1.645; testing stops at the first failure
veto_rules: no position x statistic cell worse than production by more than 2 SE (cell z < -2)
80% central-interval coverage (randomized PIT) pooled over every scored cell inside 0.70-0.90 AND nearer 0.80 than production's
mean absolute difference between the model's within-world DraftKings-point correlation and the observed residual correlation, over the pair types, no larger than production's

decision.pass: a candidate passes when its primary clears its Holm threshold and no veto trips; if several pass, the one with the largest z is RECOMMENDED. Nothing changes the week board until the owner signs off; the board stays labelled overconfident until then
decision.fail: no candidate passes: production stays, labelled; a failed test can be insufficient evidence, never proof that production is right

power.method: normal approximation off the development out-of-sample gain and its SE (2026 weeks 1-5, 79 games), scaled to 72 prospective games, at the strictest Holm threshold 2.128
power.note: power is the chance the test passes IF a candidate is better by the stated gain, never the probability that it is better; the development effects are large, so the test is well powered even at half of them

rule_on_development.note: the same rule applied to the development games, for reading only: it decides nothing

runbook: after 2027-01-13 06:00 UTC: rebuild research/data/player_weeks_2026.csv.gz with research/hist_data.py for 2026 weeks 1-18 (its raw Sleeper files; the development games, 2026 weeks 1-5, are pinned by window and do not change)
check out the registration commit's tree (a git worktree) if any frozen file has changed since; the read refuses otherwise
python3 research/nfl_wb_dist.py read -> research/data/nfl_wb_dist/read.json, read once, committed with the report's result section

production_until_then: unchanged: nfl_dfs_sim.simulate_game is the week board, labelled overconfident (pick6_ledger.WEEK_BOARD_CAVEAT); nothing imports the harness
